Second measurement, on the follow-up head f0f650a5 (map conditions already in place): the code smells cleared (go:S1192 and go:S3776 no longer reported), but gosecurity:S3649 persists with three BLOCKER findings inside Service.AddMember (tenant_service.go:711 read, :722 update twice). The rule therefore treats any query built from request-supplied values as a sink regardless of binding, so the map form alone does not satisfy it. Response: the update now targets the row that was just loaded, by its primary key, naming the columns through Select + a typed struct, so no request value reaches a column or condition position (verified by TestAddMember, TestAddMember_Duplicate, TestAddMember_OwnerIsProtected, TestRemoveMember against real MySQL). The remaining read-side sink is inherent to looking a row up by ids that came from the request and cannot be removed without either ignoring the input or marking the finding in Sonar; the latter is a maintainer disposition, not an agent action, and no suppression comment or rule exclusion was added.
